sentences.text: Jamalu Deen vs State (2025:Rj-Jd:25182) on 14 May, 2025
Author: Kuldeep Mathur

Bench: Kuldeep Mathur [2025:RJ-JD:25182]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 1143/2006 Jamalu Deen S/o Kherdeen, Aged 30 years, R/o Village Gomat,
Tehsil Pokhran, District Jaisalmer  ----Petitioner  Versus The State of Rajasthan, through PP

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Salim Khan For Respondent(s) : Mr. Narendra Gehlot, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 14/05/2025

By way of filing the present revision petition under Section 397 read with Section 401 Cr.P.C., the petitioner-accused has challenged the order/judgment dated 06.12.2006 passed by the R.H.J.S. District and Sessions Judge, Jaisalmer in Criminal Appeal No. 15/2006 affirming his conviction awarded by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pokhran in Original Criminal Case No. 114/2001 whereby the petitioner was sentenced to six months rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs.1,000/- for the offence under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 1954').

entities.text: R.H.J.S. District and Sessions Judge, Jaisalmer
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per the prosecution, on 02.09.2000, Food Inspector Mr. Sureshchandra Nagar during his usual patrolling hours saw the petitioner on a motorcycle with a tank of milk.

Thereafter, the Food Inspector asked the petitioner to produce his food license to [2025:RJ-JD:25182] (2 of 4)
[CRLR-1143/2006] which the petitioner responded that he does not possess any Food License.
The Food Inspector purchased 750 ml of milk from the petitioner and sent the same for examination to the Public Analyst.
The Public Analyst in its report found that the milk samples were adulterated and there was presence of about 33% water in the said sample.
On the basis of the report of the Public Analyst, the petitioner was prosecuted for the offence under Section 7/16 of the Act of 1954.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the sentence awarded to the petitioner has already been suspended by this Court vide order dated 13.12.2006 in Cr. Misc. Suspension of Sentence (Bail)
No. 318/06.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that since there was a time gap of 7 months between the time when the samples were collected and the time when the complaint was lodged is fatal to the case of the prosecution.

Furthermore, the counsel submitted that even though there was a huge crowd of people present when the sample was taken, the Food Inspector still called upon his subordinates to be the witness for the collection of the sample which puts a question upon his integrity and impartiality.

In the alternative, he submitted that since the occurrence relates to year 2000 and the petitioner has already served some part of the sentence awarded to him, therefore, the substantive sentence awarded to the petitioner be reduced to the period already undergone by him.

Reliance was placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Puttaswamy v State of Karnataka:2009 (1) WLC (SC) (Cri.) 623 and a [2025:RJ-JD:25182] (3 of 4)
[CRLR-1143/2006] judgment of Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Kamla Prasad v. State of Rajasthan: 2014 CriLJ 2582.

entities.text: Puttaswamy v State of Karnataka:2009 (1) WLC (SC) (Cri.) 623
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Kamla Prasad v. State of Rajasthan: 2014 CriLJ 2582
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the learned Courts below have rightly awarded the sentence against the petitioner.
There is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgments/orders and therefore, the same do not call for any interference by this Court in exercise of the revisional jurisdiction.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the record of the case.
This Court does not agree with the contentions of the learned counsel for the petitioner.

However, in the opinion of this Court since the incident relates to the year 2000 and the petitioner has suffered the agony and trauma of protracted trial for about 25 years coupled with the fact that the petitioner has spent some period in custody, it will be just and proper if the sentence awarded by the trial court for the offence under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is reduced to the period already undergone by the petitioner while directing him to deposit the fine amount if not already deposited.
In the result, the revision petition is partly allowed.

While maintaining the petitioner's conviction, his sentence for the offence 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 is hereby reduced to the period already undergone by him.
The petitioner is already on bail vide order dated 13.12.2006 in Cr. Misc. Suspension of Sentence (Bail) No. 318/06.

entities.text: Cr. Misc. Suspension of Sentence (Bail) No. 318/06
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: He need not surrender.
His bail bonds stand discharged accordingly.
All pending applications, if any, stand [2025:RJ-JD:25182] (4 of 4) [CRLR-1143/2006] disposed of.
The records of the trial court as well as appellate court be sent back forthwith.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 24-divya/-
